query: What signals indicate a hardware incident is in the anomaly window?

per_column.name: failure_symptom
per_column.rationale: Directly relevant to identifying hardware incident signals; provides a strong categorical axis (connection_failure, disk_failure, overheating, etc.) to group/model on. Samples show sound readings: 'connection to MySQL server' -> connection_failure, software-install rows -> Unknown, which is correct silent-row behaviour.

per_column.name: incident_scope_context
per_column.rationale: Scope (single_workstation vs server_infrastructure vs network_segment) is a genuine grouping axis useful for characterising incidents in an anomaly window. 'MySQL server' -> server_infrastructure is well warranted; software-install rows -> Unknown is appropriate.

per_column.name: technician_assignment_stability
per_column.rationale: A boolean stability flag could plausibly be a signal (reassignment churn), giving some analytical leverage. However groundedness is questionable: the source text/columns shown (short_description, timestamps) do not clearly support a true/false stability determination, and no evidence of assignment history is exposed. Values default to False without visible justification.

per_column.name: caller_repeat_status
per_column.rationale: Repeat-caller status is a reasonable anomaly signal (recurring hardware failures). Derivable in principle from caller_id frequency, an original column. But two identical software-install rows for the same description yield 'first_time' and later 'repeat_caller' inconsistently across samples, and the value isn't clearly grounded in the shown source text, lowering confidence.

per_column.name: software_update_interference
per_column.rationale: A boolean about update interference is somewhat relevant since updates can precipitate incidents, giving a distinguishing axis. Grounding is partial: 'Unable to install new update on system' -> True is well supported, but for a hardware-focused query this is a weaker, mostly-negative flag.

judge.rationale: The added columns give several genuine new axes (symptom type, scope, repeat behaviour, update linkage) directly relevant to detecting hardware-incident signals, so usefulness is solid. Groundedness is strongest for failure_symptom and incident_scope_context, which show sound extraction from short_description and appropriate 'Unknown' on silent rows. The two boolean columns (technician_assignment_stability, software_update_interference) and caller_repeat_status are weaker: their values are not clearly supported by the visible source text and appear to default heavily to False/first_time without shown evidence, with some cross-row inconsistency. No overt hallucination of invented specifics observed in the samples.
